criterion: AC1 long-input dimension: p95 CPU latency at inputs up to 4k tokens

window.swept_coverage_is_not_contiguous: With 24 windows of 94 at stride 62, the first 23 windows cover a contiguous 1,458 tokens and planWindowStarts reassigns the 24th start to the tail, so coverage is 1,552 tokens in TWO pieces with a hole between them. The tail is always read; the middle of a long document is not. A payload buried mid-document is outside both arms.

route_cap.note: lib/guard/constants.ts caps accepted guard text at 8000 chars, which this tokenizer turns into ~1384 content tokens. An input of 4,096 tokens is therefore REFUSED by every guard route before any tier sees it. The spec's 4k ceiling is unreachable through the product surface, independently of the model window.

as_deployed_sweep_off.honest_reading: p95 at 4092 content tokens is 304.076ms against a 50ms target, and only 254 of 4092 tokens (6.2%) were scored — the rest were discarded before the forward pass. Coverage falls from 99.6% to 6.2% across this sweep while latency stays in the same band (272.189ms at one window, 304.076ms at 4k): the cost is essentially INDEPENDENT of input length, because the forward pass sees 254 tokens either way. That is the whole problem. A figure that does not move when you hand it 16x more text is not a measurement of 4k-token latency, and must not be recorded as meeting a 4k-token target. No claim is made here about the direction of the residual difference: at 25 samples on a shared host the run-to-run jitter is larger than the gap.

sweep_on_counterfactual.honest_reading: With the sweep on, 24 windows cover 1552 of 4092 tokens (37.9%) at p95 2458.252ms, 8.1x the truncating arm and 49x the target. Coverage is capped by ML_ONNX_MAX_WINDOWS (24) and is not contiguous, so the middle of the document is unread even here.

detection_columns_are_not_recall.note: Every row carries a benign CONTROL of identical length with the payload removed. Where the control also flags, the payload is NOT attributable and the flag is a false positive on business prose, which is what this model does at wide windows. Read tailPayloadAttributable, never predictedLabel alone. These are single-row probes of the window question and are not a recall measurement.

benign_long_prose_false_positives.finding: 10 of 10 payload-free business-prose controls were flagged, in BOTH arms and at every length from 255 to 4,092 tokens. Ordinary logistics, contract and deployment prose is labelled PII. Two consequences. First, this fixture family cannot demonstrate tail-payload detection at all: the decision is already non-SAFE before the payload is added, so attribution is UNMEASURABLE here regardless of coverage. Second, it is the same defect AC6 measures as a 23% real-path FPR, reproduced on a handful of hand-written rows — long benign text is a systematic false positive for this artifact, not a rare one.
benign_long_prose_false_positives.caveat: Five hand-written sentences repeated to length. This is a reproduction of a known failure mode, not an FPR measurement; cite eval-acceptance.py for FPR.

verdict.why: AC1's 4k-token dimension FAILS in every available configuration, for three independent reasons. (1) As deployed, 6.2% of a 4k input is scored, so its 304.076ms p95 is not a 4k measurement. (2) With the sweep on, coverage rises to 37.9% but p95 is 2458.252ms against a 50ms target. (3) A 4k-token input is ~23686 chars and every guard route rejects anything over 8000, so it never reaches a tier at all. The 256-token window is architectural, not a setting: closing this needs a longer-context encoder, not a flag flip.

limitations: Inference only: excludes the rules tier, semantic veto, transport and queueing. End-to-end product latency is HIGHER than every figure here.
Batch one on CPU, this host, other processes possible. Not a load test and not a throughput measurement.

Run-to-run jitter on this host is tens of ms at 25 samples — larger than the gap between adjacent token budgets in the truncating arm. Read the BAND and the order of magnitude, not the third digit, and do not infer a trend from neighbouring rows. The verdict does not depend on it: every figure misses 50ms by at least 5x.
Coverage is the backend's own raw.tokensScored / raw.contentTokens.
One fixture family (business prose + tail payload). The detection columns are single-row probes of the window question, NOT a recall measurement — do not cite them as recall.
GPU is not measured at all; the spec's 15ms GPU target remains UNMEASURED here.
